prompt: Stage 4-4 carousel, level 8, 47 HP, you pick third. Your 4-cost AD carry is 1-star with two items and you plan to roll for it at 4-5. The carousel shows a second copy of that carry holding a random defensive component, and separately the exact AD component that completes its BIS third item, carried by a 1-cost. Which do you take?

options.label: The carry copy with the defensive component: 4 gold of unit, pool progress, and a component anyway
The exact BIS component on the 1-cost: the third item is a damage multiplier you cannot roll for
Either is fine; take whichever is closer when the carousel unlocks

explanation:
Count the value. The carry copy is a 4-cost unit (4 gold if you sold it) that moves your 4-5 rolldown from "find two copies" to "find one", which at roughly 10% per slot for one specific 4-cost is a saving of 15-20 gold of rolling on average, and it comes with a component you can combine into a tank item for the bruiser. The BIS component is 1 component of value plus a 1-cost you will sell for 1 gold; it completes a third item that is a multiplier on a 1-star carry, and a 1-star carry with three items still loses to a 2-star carry with two.

At 47 HP on a 2-loss streak the 2-star is the stabiliser, not the third item. Late carousels are where units outvalue components precisely because the unit is the one thing the shop makes expensive. "Either" is not a position; carousel picks at stage 4 decide placements.
principle: From stage 4 on, a copy of your itemised carry on the carousel is worth more than any component, BIS included.
commonMistake: Grabbing the BIS component because it is the item you have been waiting for, and rolling 20 extra gold at 4-5 to find the copy you left on the carousel.
